palais-maimun.fait: This palace of the Sultan of Deli, in Medan, blends elements of Malay, Muslim, Spanish, Indian, and Italian cultures.

baiturrahman.fait: This mosque in Banda Aceh has become an even stronger symbol since the 2004 tsunami, which it came through intact.

merapi.fait: This volcano near Yogyakarta, considered the most active and most dangerous in Indonesia, periodically produces pyroclastic flows.

semeru.fait: This volcano, the highest point in eastern Java, is classified as a “gray volcano” because its eruptions are mostly explosive.

iles-gili.fait: Saying “Gili Islands” is a misnomer: “gili” already means “island” in Sasak, the language of most of Lombok's inhabitants.

ujung-kulon.fait: This national park, at the western tip of the island of Java, also includes the Krakatoa group of volcanic islands.

tanjung-puting.fait: During feedings in this park, female orangutans arrive with their young and peel bananas with their lips.

charminar.fait: This Hyderabad monument, which houses a mosque, bears a name meaning “four columns”; it is the city's best-known building.

mahabodhi.fait: Behind this temple stands the Bodhi Tree, under which Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment.

sanchi.fait: This Buddhist site has no link to the historical Buddha; fallen into oblivion, it was rediscovered in 1818 by a British officer.

mehrangarh.fait: Nicknamed “the magnificent fort,” it overlooks Jodhpur and houses several richly decorated palaces and many courtyards.

cst-mumbai.fait: This station, formerly called Victoria Terminus, is one of the busiest in the country and houses the headquarters of the Central Railway network.

kaziranga.fait: This park is home to two-thirds of all existing Indian rhinoceroses, as well as the highest density of tigers in the world.

national-museum-sg.fait: Opened in 1887, it is Singapore's oldest museum; its mission is to preserve and pass on the history and stories of the country.

peranakan-museum.fait: Housed in a former school, this museum, the first of its kind in the world, presents Peranakan culture, also known as Baba-Nyonya.

pi-mai.fait: This New Year linked to Theravada Buddhism is a water festival, celebrated at the hottest time of the year, shortly before the rainy season.

gosainkunda.fait: According to legend, Shiva dug this lake with his trident to find cold water after drinking a poison.

musee-national-kh.fait: All photography is prohibited in this museum, which holds one of the most important collections of Khmer art.

prasat-kravan.fait: Unusually, this sanctuary was commissioned not by a king but by high dignitaries, hence its location somewhat apart from the center.

wat-chaiwatthanaram.fait: This Ayutthaya temple was built on the model of an Angkor temple, in honor of the king's mother, or perhaps to celebrate a victory over the Khmers.

bang-pa-in.fait: This summer palace of the kings blends Chinese, Gothic Revival, and Italian styles; a pavilion stands there in the middle of a lake.

khao-san.fait: This Bangkok neighborhood, known for its budget guesthouses and as a backpacker hangout, is also called “T-shirt street.”

bateau-longue-queue.fait: This traditional boat is usually powered by a car engine mounted outboard, connected to the propeller by a long shaft.

wat-phra-singh.fait: The name of this Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, in northern Thailand, means “the temple of the Lion Lord.”

dong-ho.fait: These prints are painted woodcuts, born in the village of Đông Hồ, in Bắc Ninh province.

citadelle-ho.fait: This citadel of large cut stones was built according to feng shui; destroyed by the Ming in 1407, it lies in ruins, except for its four gates.

cat-ba.fait: This island, the largest in Ha Long Bay, is home to a national park that brings together many endemic animal and plant species.

ba-be.fait: This lake in Ba Be National Park, in Bac Kan, is the largest natural freshwater lake in Vietnam.

thatbyinnyu.fait: This Bagan temple has no central pillar, and its platform served as a monastery: the monks lived in corridors around its edge.

sulamani.fait: This Bagan temple is modeled on the Thatbyinnyu; its tower, partly toppled by an earthquake, was rebuilt in the 1990s.

vigan.fait: This town, founded in the 16th century, with its cobbled streets, is an almost intact example of a Spanish colonial town in Asia.

coron.fait: Around this island in Palawan province, Japanese wrecks sunk during World War II attract many divers.

kraton-yogya.fait: This royal palace, called a kraton, is still the seat of the Sultan of Yogyakarta, the city where it stands, in Indonesia.

vallee-baliem.fait: This valley in the mountains of Papua is mainly inhabited by Papuans of the Dani ethnic group; its main town is Wamena.

kerinci.fait: This volcano, the highest point on Sumatra and one of the most active in the country, remains a popular destination: its eruptions are not very violent.

the-assam.fait: This strong-tasting black tea is sometimes part of the blends sold as “breakfast tea,” such as Irish Breakfast Tea.

feni.fait: This liquor from Goa is made from the juice of coconut or cashew, a Brazilian nut introduced by Portuguese colonists.

madhubani.fait: This style of painting, also called Mithila painting, is practiced in that region of the state of Bihar, in India.

filter-coffee.fait: This coffee, called kaapi in southern India, is cut with about 20% roasted chicory and brewed through a traditional Indian filter.

tanjore.fait: These brightly colored paintings mainly depict Hindu gods and saints; the style has also spread to glass painting.

kambala.fait: This annual buffalo race enlivens the Karnataka coast from November to March, even in small, isolated villages.

sattriya.fait: This classical dance, also called Sattriya Nritya, originates from Assam, a state in northeastern India.

rani-ki-vav.fait: It is called “the Queen's stepwell”: this baoli is located in the town of Patan, in Gujarat.

chand-baori.fait: This stepwell in Rajasthan, nearly thirty meters deep, descends over thirteen levels of steps; it is one of the largest baolis in India.

living-root-bridges.fait: These bridges are made from the living aerial roots of rubber fig trees; the Khasi and Jaintia peoples of the Shillong Plateau, in particular, use them.

golconde.fait: This “fort” is actually a ruined fortified city, a former royal capital, whose lower town is threatened by the expansion of Hyderabad.

elephanta.fait: These temples carved into a cliff, on an island off Bombay, preserve a monumental set of sculptures.

pecel.fait: This salad from Java, topped with peanut sauce, is also popular in Suriname, home to a large Javanese community.

nagasari.fait: This steamed Javanese cake, made of rice flour, coconut milk, and sugar, hides a slice of banana.

oncom.fait: This staple food of the Sundanese of West Java is, like tempeh, prepared by fermentation using molds.

semur.fait: This stew of meat braised in a thick brown sauce has as its main ingredient kecap manis, a sweet soy sauce.

barfi.fait: The name of this Indian confection made with condensed milk comes from the Persian word barf, meaning “snow.”

dahi-vada.fait: This snack is made of vada, ball-shaped flour fritters, which are soaked in thick yogurt.

bebinca.fait: This layered cake, a legacy of the Indo-Portuguese cuisine of Goa, is especially popular during the Christmas season.

soan-papdi.fait: This crisp, flaky dessert used to be sold loose in paper cones; today it is found in packaged cubes.

aloo-tikki.fait: This patty of boiled, spiced potatoes, served hot with chutneys, can be found at almost every chaat stall in Delhi.

bonda.fait: This fritter of mashed potatoes and chickpea flour comes in sweet or savory versions, depending on the region of southern India.

kadhi.fait: This yogurt curry, with a sauce thickened with chickpea flour, contains vegetable fritters called pakora.

aloo-paratha.fait: This flatbread stuffed with spiced potatoes, cooked on a griddle with butter or ghee, is a much-loved breakfast.

kachori.fait: This spicy snack is a ball of dough stuffed with peas, fried in oil, and popular in many states of India.

aloo-chaat.fait: The name of this street food combines aloo, “potato,” and chaat, derived from a Hindi word meaning “tasty.”

gujia.fait: This fried pastry, with a shell similar to that of the samosa, is filled with dried fruits, khoya, and coconut.

boondi.fait: This very sweet fried snack made from chickpea flour keeps for about a week, an asset in the arid region of Rajasthan.

imarti.fait: This confection is urad bean batter fried in the shape of a circular flower, then soaked in sugar syrup.

kozhakkattai.fait: This rice-flour dumpling from southern India, usually sweet, hides a filling of grated coconut, jaggery, or candied jackfruit.

murukku.fait: Its name means “twisted” in Tamil: this fried snack of rice and urad bean flour is eaten especially for Diwali.

bhakri.fait: This round unleavened bread, coarser than an ordinary roti, can be soft or as hard as khakhra.

khakhra.fait: This thin, crunchy cracker, common among Jains, is made one at a time by hand and then roasted.

chikki.fait: This candy is most often made from peanuts and jaggery; its varieties, with sesame or puffed rice, are named after their ingredients.

pathiri.fait: This rice flour flatbread of the Mappila people of Kerala is sometimes soaked in coconut milk to keep it soft.

papadum.fait: This fried flatbread, made from urad bean flour, is eaten as an appetizer or a snack, in India as well as in Sri Lanka.

pachisi.fait: The name of this game is said to come from pachis, “twenty-five”: the highest possible score when throwing the cowrie shells used as dice.

naem.fait: This fermented pork sausage, with a sour taste, keeps only a short time and is often eaten raw after fermentation.

sauce-chili-sucree.fait: This sauce, called nam chim kai in Thailand, owes its thick consistency to the frequent addition of cornstarch.

banh-bao.fait: This steamed stuffed bun, inspired by Chinese baozi, often contains a hard-boiled egg and sausage.

bando.fait: This Burmese martial art is an unarmed self-defense system based on the behavior of animals.

chutney.fait: This often sweet-and-sour sauce accompanies dishes of Indian cuisine, but can also enhance foie gras.

puri.fait: This unleavened bread is eaten for breakfast, as a snack or as a light meal, in India as in the rest of the subcontinent.

chaat.fait: The name of this savory snack, sold from street carts, comes from Hindi words meaning “delicacy” and “to lick.”

batata-vada.fait: In the name of this fritter, the word batata may come from the Portuguese colonies on India’s west coast.

ada-kerala.fait: These sweet rice parcels, steamed in a banana leaf, are offered to worshippers in the temples of Kerala.

chaturanga.fait: Its name means “four limbs”: this ancient Indian strategy game is sometimes seen as one of the ancestors of chess.

serpents-echelles.fait: This game is said to come from an ancient Hindu game in which the ladders represented good deeds and the snakes bad ones, on the path to heaven.

mangalsutra.fait: This necklace, often of black beads, is tied around the bride’s neck by the groom and is then worn throughout the marriage.

gatka.fait: This Sikh martial art is practiced with wooden sticks that simulate swords, both as a sport and as a demonstration at weddings.

pacu-jawi.fait: The jockey holds on to the tails of two bulls, but no official winner is declared: spectators judge the animals and can buy the best ones.

cha-lua.fait: This pork sausage wrapped in banana leaves changes name: chả lụa in the South, giò lụa in the North of Vietnam.

rajput-painting.fait: These schools of painting grew up in the royal courts of Rajasthan; those of the Himalayan foothills are called “Pahari painting.”

diya.fait: This oil lamp is usually made of clay; its cotton wick soaks in ghee or in vegetable oil.

nilgiri-tea.fait: A tea from these hills set a world record at 600 dollars per kilo, at the first tea auction held in Las Vegas.

dum-aloo.fait: This Kashmiri curry first sautés small whole potatoes, then lets them simmer over low heat in a spicy sauce.

sittang.fait: This river flows through Naypyidaw, the capital of Myanmar, but the tidal bore at its mouth and its strong currents make it poorly suited to navigation.

musee-civilisations-asiatiques.fait: This museum presents the cultures of China and of South, Southeast and West Asia, where Singapore’s main ethnic groups come from.

musee-art-sg.fait: This museum, the first in Singapore devoted entirely to contemporary visual arts, also organizes the Singapore Biennale.

tunku-abdul-rahman.fait: This national park in Sabah is mostly marine: it groups five islands, including Gaya and Sapi, off Kota Kinabalu.

musee-sarawak.fait: This museum, the oldest in Borneo, holds two specimens of the bay cat; it was funded notably by the White Rajah Charles Brooke.

bundala.fait: This park, where migratory waterbirds including the greater flamingo spend the winter, was Sri Lanka’s first wetland designated a Ramsar site.

musee-colombo.fait: This museum, the largest in Sri Lanka, holds the throne and crown of the kings of Kandy, as well as traditional costumes.

phrumsengla.fait: This park in central Bhutan is cut in two by the main east–west highway and includes the Thrumshing La pass, which gave it its former name.

ghi.fait: This clarified butter, born in the Indian subcontinent, is also found in Arab cuisines, from the Levant to Egypt and the Maghreb.

bhut-jolokia.fait: Nicknamed the “ghost pepper,” this cultivar from Assam was listed in Guinness World Records as the hottest chili pepper in the world.

makruk.fait: This close relative of chess is played in Thailand; like its Western cousin, it probably descends from Indian chaturanga.

ratu-boko.fait: Unlike the nearby temples of Prambanan, this site on Java seems to have been a place of residence, whose exact function remains unknown.

kheer.fait: This sweet rice pudding is also the dish most often chosen to wean the infant during the annaprashana ceremony.

chapati.fait: This wheat flatbread from northern India is traditionally made without leavening; in French, usage wavers between “le” and “la” chapati.

mie-goreng.fait: Its name means “fried noodles”: this dish is found in almost every restaurant and stall across the Indonesian archipelago.

serabi.fait: This pancake made of rice flour and coconut is mostly eaten sweet, often with a thick golden-brown coconut sugar syrup.

gir.fait: This park in Gujarat is the only place in the world, outside Africa, where lions can still be found in the wild.

vada.fait: This savory snack from southern India comes as a sandwich, in a version marinated in yogurt, or made with potatoes.

maha-shivaratri.fait: According to one account, this night of fasting and meditation celebrates the day Shiva drank the poison of destruction to save the world.

vaisakhi.fait: This harvest festival, usually on April 13, also marks the new year in most calendars of northern India.

janmashtami.fait: This festival celebrates the birth of Krishna; its name means “birth of the eighth,” notably because Krishna is the eighth avatar of Vishnu.

katar.fait: This dagger from southern India has a horizontal grip that allows thrusting blows capable of piercing armor.

canyon-tara.fait: Carved by the Tara River, which flows through Durmitor National Park, this canyon is the deepest in Europe.

cetinje-monastere.fait: This Orthodox monastery in Cetinje is the seat of the Metropolitanate of Montenegro and the Littoral, part of the Serbian Orthodox Church.

herceg-novi.fait: This resort town on the Bay of Kotor, very close to Croatia, is called Castelnuovo in Italian.

hotel-ville-tallinn.fait: This medieval town hall, built in the 15th century in the late Gothic style, still stands on its square in Tallinn.

kuressaare.fait: This castle once belonged to a bishop: it is also called the Episcopal Castle, and its German name is Schloss Arensburg.

haapsalu.fait: This castle is also a cathedral, Saint Nicholas, seat of an archdiocese of the Estonian Lutheran Church; the diocese dates back to 1228.

kopu.fait: This lighthouse, run by the Maritime Administration, is often seen as the symbol of the Estonian island of Hiiumaa.

lukomir.fait: This village in the municipality of Konjic, in Herzegovina, had only 41 inhabitants at the Bosnian census.

jajce.fait: This town has applied for UNESCO World Heritage status for its ensemble, which is both natural and architectural.

trencin.fait: This 11th-century fortified castle overlooks both the town of Trenčín and the Váh River, in northwestern Slovakia.

krasna-horka.fait: Built in the 14th century in southeastern Slovakia, this castle, mentioned in writing as early as 1333, was declared a national monument in 1966.

levoca.fait: This town in the Prešov Region has three other names: Leutschau in German, Lőcse in Hungarian and Lewocza in Polish.

strbske.fait: This glacial lake in the High Tatras stays covered with ice 155 days a year; it gave its name to a ski resort.

lomnicky.fait: Long thought to be the highest peak in the Carpathians, it is the only one in the High Tatras that can be reached by cable car.

paradis-slovaque.fait: This park has more than 350 caves, but only one is open to the public: the Dobšiná Ice Cave.

strecno.fait: This medieval castle overlooks a strategic gorge: its position allowed it to collect and guard the toll on the pass.

sainte-anne-vilnius.fait: This late Gothic Catholic church is one of the most representative monuments of the historic center of Vilnius.

palanga-ambre.fait: Nearly 15,000 pieces of amber in this museum contain insects, spiders or plants that became trapped inside.

raudone.fait: This castle, which belonged to King Sigismund II, was acquired much later by the Russian prince Platon Zubov, whose family transformed it once again.

birzai.fait: This castle stands on the site of a Radziwiłł residence destroyed by the Swedish army during the Great Northern War.

plaosnik.fait: This archaeological site in Ohrid, located below Samuel's Fortress, is also a holy site being restored to its original state.

treskavec.fait: Perched on a rocky plateau near the summit of Mount Zlatovrv, this monastery burned down: apart from its church, it is now only a ruin.

galicica.fait: The mountains of this park separate two lakes, Ohrid and Prespa; the former is considered the oldest lake in Europe.

saint-sava.fait: The second-largest Orthodox church in the world, this Belgrade basilica also has the largest dome mosaic in the world.

ravanica.fait: This Orthodox monastery in the Morava Valley is on the list of Cultural Monuments of Exceptional Importance of Serbia.

manasija.fait: This Orthodox monastery near Despotovac has a second name, Resava, and is one of the monuments of exceptional importance of Serbia.

mileseva.fait: This monastery near Prijepolje is the seat of the Eparchy of Mileševa and is still home to a religious community.

viminacium.fait: Capital of Moesia Superior, this Roman city was ravaged by Bleda, king of the Huns, then destroyed for good during the Slavic invasions.

krusedol.fait: The Serbian despots Đurađ Branković and Stefan Lazarević are buried in this monastery, which is now home to nuns.

velika-planina.fait: On this mountain pasture, herders spend the summer in one-room wooden houses, and the small ski resort is best suited to beginners.

logar.fait: This valley corresponds to the upper course of the Savinja, which rises in the Kamnik Alps; it also forms a village of scattered houses.

secovlje.fait: Salt is still produced here the traditional way and sold as Piran salt; these saltworks have been operating since the 13th century.

place-preseren.fait: This square in Ljubljana is named after France Prešeren, who can be considered the national poet of Slovenia.

stricna.fait: Dissolved by Joseph II, this Cistercian abbey regained a monastic life in 1898; it is still active.

osum.fait: This gorge is named after the Osum, the river that also flows through the town of Berat; it is protected within Mount Tomorr National Park.

chateau-berat.fait: Dating mostly from the 13th century, this fortress houses both Byzantine churches and Ottoman mosques; it can only be entered from the south.

voskopoje.fait: This small town in southern Albania has three names: Voskopojë in Albanian, Moscopole in Aromanian and Moschopolis in Greek.

chateau-riga.fait: This fortress on the banks of the Daugava serves as the official residence and workplace of the President of the Republic of Latvia.

maison-chat.fait: This building in Riga, built in 1909 by the architect Friedrich Scheffel, features elements of the Art Nouveau style.

jurmala.fait: This town in Latvia, at the head of the Gulf of Riga, was once called Rigastrand in German.

remparts-dubrovnik.fait: These stone walls surrounding Dubrovnik were never breached by an enemy army in the Middle Ages.

saint-marc-zagreb.fait: This parish church stands on St. Mark's Square, in Gradec, in the upper town of Zagreb, called Gornji Grad in Croatian.

stari-grad.fait: On the island of Hvar, this agricultural plain still bears the mark of ancient Greek colonization in the 4th century BC.

tarator.fait: This cold soup of yogurt, cucumber, garlic and walnuts is sometimes served with ice cubes, as a starter or as a side salad.

kazanlak-tombe.fait: This Thracian funerary monument, of the tholos type, was built near the town of Kazanlak, in central Bulgaria.

prohodna.fait: The ceiling of this cave is pierced by naturally formed holes, nicknamed the “Eyes of God.”

uspenski.fait: This Helsinki cathedral is the seat of the Orthodox diocese of the capital, within the Orthodox Church of Finland.

petajavesi.fait: This old Lutheran wooden church in west-central Finland has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994.

oulanka.fait: This 270 km² park, located on the Arctic Circle, borders Paanajärvi National Park in Russia.

rubjerg.fait: Threatened with falling into the sea under the pressure of the sand, this lighthouse was moved inland in 2019.

gefion.fait: This fountain shows the goddess Gefjon on a plow pulled by her four sons, turned into bulls.

borsen.fait: This building is known for its twisted spire formed by entwined dragon tails; a fire devastated it in 2024.

trelleborg.fait: This perfectly circular Viking rampart is divided into equal sections by paths that cross at right angles.

notre-sauveur.fait: This Baroque church is famous for its spiral spire and its external spiral staircase, which offers a wide view over Copenhagen.

den-gamle-by.fait: This open-air museum in Aarhus recreates old Danish houses; a few even show Denmark as it was in 1970.

ribe.fait: In the Middle Ages, this town in Jutland was among the most important ports on the North Sea; it has kept its fishermen's houses.

seljalandsfoss.fait: You can walk behind this waterfall; at sunset, the light gives the water an orange hue.

svartifoss.fait: Its Icelandic name literally means “the black waterfall”; it is located in Skaftafell National Park.

godafoss.fait: This waterfall on the Skjálfandafljót river, one of the most famous in Iceland, is 12 meters high and 30 meters wide.

surtsey.fait: Born from an undersea eruption in 1963, this island is closed to the public: only scientists may go there to observe the life taking hold.

matthias.fait: Converted into a mosque during the Ottoman occupation, this Budapest church was used for the coronation of several monarchs.

vajdahunyad.fait: This Budapest castle brings together pavilions in the styles that shaped Hungary; its silhouette is inspired by a castle in Transylvania.

opera-budapest.fait: This Neo-Renaissance opera house in Budapest is called the Hungarian State Opera and is home to the national opera of Hungary.

tihany.fait: This Benedictine abbey, on the shores of Lake Balaton, was founded in 1055 by King Andrew I.

eger.fait: This former fortress overlooking the old town of Eger was one of the key sites of the siege led in 1552 by the Ottoman army.

borgund.fait: Dated through the study of its wood, this stave church, probably built before 1200, is considered the best preserved in Norway.

heddal.fait: The largest stave church in Norway still serves as a parish church; animal heads adorn its gables.

nidaros.fait: This Trondheim cathedral was built over the tomb of King Saint Olaf; it is the northernmost medieval cathedral.

trollstigen.fait: The name of this mountain road literally means “the Troll's path”; it links Åndalsnes to Valldal.

roros.fait: This town in Trøndelag county, in the Gauldalen region, is on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

flam.fait: This railway line links Flåm to Myrdal: its steep gradient and its scenery have made it a major tourist attraction.

naeroyfjord.fait: This fjord, a branch of the Sognefjord, is a World Heritage Site together with the Geirangerfjord under the name West Norwegian Fjords.

alta.fait: These carvings in northern Norway are the country's only prehistoric site selected by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

cathedrale-wawel.fait: This Kraków cathedral serves as a national sanctuary: kings, queens, poets and heroes of Poland are buried there.

barbacane.fait: This Gothic defensive structure is part of the medieval fortifications of the city of Kraków.

neptune-gdansk.fait: This 17th-century fountain, commissioned by Mayor Bartłomiej Schachmann, stands on the Long Market, at the entrance to Artus Court.

foret-tordue.fait: In this Pomeranian wood, about four hundred pines have trunks bent at a right angle just above the ground, before growing upward again.

hotel-ville-wroclaw.fait: This old town hall stands at the center of Wrocław, the largest city in western Poland, called Breslau in German.

lazienki.fait: This Warsaw palace, built in Łazienki Park, is also called in Polish the “Palace on the Isle” or the “Palace on the Water.”

moszna.fait: This fairy-tale castle dates back to the 18th century, but older cellars may be the remains of a presumed Templar fortress.

zamosc.fait: This town is the seat of a district it does not belong to: it forms a separate district on its own.

giewont.fait: This peak in the Tatras has three summits, the Small, the Great and the Long Giewont; the climb requires good physical fitness.

pelisor.fait: This Art Nouveau castle, built by King Carol I on the estate of Peleș Castle, in Sinaia, is now a museum.

transalpina.fait: This road, the highest in Romania, was built during World War I; snow usually closes it from mid-October to mid-June.

mogosoaia.fait: This palace is named after the widow of Mogoș, a squire who owned the land; it served as a setting for the film “Sept hommes et une garce.”

laure-trinite.fait: This major Orthodox monastery is in Sergiev Posad, a town called Zagorsk from 1930 to 1991, about 75 km northeast of Moscow.

novodievitchi.fait: The name of this Moscow convent is said, according to legend, to come from the young girls who took cows to graze at this spot.

goum.fait: Its name is a Russian acronym meaning “Main Universal Store”: it is an upscale shopping center on Red Square, in Moscow.

klioutchevskoi.fait: This volcano in Kamchatka, the highest point in Siberia, formed about 6,000 years ago on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

elbrouz.fait: According to one legend, Prometheus was chained to the two peaks of this Caucasus volcano for giving fire to humankind.

nerl.nom: Church of the Intercession on the Nerl
nerl.fait: This white stone church, renowned for the harmony of its proportions, is probably the first in Russia dedicated to the Intercession of the Mother of God.

solovki.fait: This Russian Orthodox monastery stands on the Solovetsky Islands, on the White Sea, in northwestern Russia.

palais-catherine.fait: This 18th-century Baroque palace is in Pushkin, formerly Tsarskoye Selo, whose name means “the Tsar's village.”

riddarholmen.fait: This former abbey in Stockholm houses the tombs of most Swedish monarchs from the 17th to the 20th century; since 1922, the royal family has been buried at Haga.

uppsala.fait: This cathedral, the largest in Scandinavia along with Trondheim's, notably holds the remains of the naturalist Carl Linnaeus.

visby.fait: This Gotland rampart grew out of a simple tower that protected the harbor; the wall was later built because of a conflict between Visby and the rest of the island.

gripsholm.fait: This castle houses the national portrait collection of the Swedish state; at its entrance, two runestones recall Ingvar's Viking expedition.

gota.fait: This early 19th-century canal crosses southern Sweden, from Gothenburg to the Baltic Sea, passing through the large lakes Vänern and Vättern.

tanum.fait: These drawings carved into the rock, on the west coast of Sweden, in the province of Bohuslän, are among the most famous in the country.

lund.fait: This building is the largest Romanesque cathedral in Scandinavia; with 700,000 visitors in 2008, it is the main tourist attraction in Lund.

palais-royal-stockholm.fait: This palace, on the Norrström in the old town of Stockholm, is the official residence of the monarchs of Sweden.

hluboka.fait: This Neo-Gothic castle is in the town of Hluboká nad Vltavou, in Czechia; its German name is Frauenberg.

telc.fait: This small town in the Vysočina Region owes its fame to its historic center, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

macocha.fait: This abyss in the Moravian Karst is the deepest of its kind in Central Europe; it attracts visitors, but also cavers and divers.

adrspach.fait: This rock nature reserve, established in 1933 in Czechia, is called Adersbach-Weckelsdorfer Felsenstadt in German.

petrin.fait: This 63-meter-high steel tower overlooks the city of Prague; in Czech, it is called Petřínská rozhledna.

strahov.fait: Founded in the 12th century, this Prague monastery is the oldest Premonstratensian monastery in Bohemia and houses a famous Baroque library.

vieille-nouvelle.fait: This Prague synagogue is the oldest still in use in Europe; the one in Erfurt is older, but it is now only a museum.

konopiste.fait: This castle was the last residence of Archduke Franz Ferdinand before his assassination in Sarajevo; the bullet that killed him is on display there.

laure-grottes.fait: This major Ukrainian Orthodox monastery, located in the city of Kyiv, is also known as the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra.

opera-lviv.fait: This opera house, built at the end of the 19th century as the Grand Theater, now bears the name of the soprano Solomiya Krushelnytska.

sofiyivka.fait: This botanical garden in the city of Uman was founded by Count Stanisław Potocki; it is one of the Seven Wonders of Ukraine.

khortytsia.fait: This island, 12 kilometers long, is the longest and largest on the Dnieper; it is in Zaporizhzhia, downstream of a hydroelectric dam.

hoverla.fait: The highest mountain in Ukraine, this Carpathian peak holds on its eastern slope the main source of the Prut River.

synevyr.fait: This lake in the west of the country, one of the largest in Ukraine, regularly changes its appearance depending on weather conditions.

porte-doree-kiev.fait: This gate opened into the historic fortress of the old town of Kyiv; it is now one of the city's monuments.

palanok.fait: This castle, called Munkács vára in Hungarian and Plankenburg in German, is a complex of fortifications that now houses a museum.

opera-odessa.fait: The acoustics of this opera house allow a whisper on the stage to be heard from any part of the hall.

saint-vladimir-kiev.fait: This Kyiv cathedral, dedicated to Vladimir the Great, was consecrated in the presence of Emperor Nicholas II and Empress Alexandra.

sebilj.fait: This Sarajevo fountain, built in 1891 in the Baščaršija quarter, is on the provisional list of the country's national monuments.

haggadah.fait: This Hebrew manuscript, one of the most richly illuminated, is a national monument of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but it was made in Spain in the 14th century.

mosquee-empereur.fait: Built in the 16th century, this mosque is the very first one built in Sarajevo; it is one of the national monuments of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

tvrdos.fait: This Serbian Orthodox monastery, founded in the 15th century, is in Bosnia and Herzegovina, within the territory of the city of Trebinje.

demanova.fait: This cave is one of the two Demänovská caves, located in the valley of the same name in Slovakia, 12 km from the town of Liptovský Mikuláš.

porte-michel.fait: This gate is the only one of the four gates in the walls of Bratislava to have survived; it is named after a suburb and a St. Michael's church outside the walls.

cerveny-kamen.fait: The name of this castle in the Little Carpathians literally means “red stone”; it rises above the village of Častá.

mustafa-pacha.fait: This Ottoman mosque overlooks the Old Bazaar of Skopje; in its courtyard, a türbe still holds the sarcophagus of a daughter of Mustafa Pasha.

arabati-baba.fait: This Sufi monastery in Tetovo was built around the tomb of a dervish, Sersem Ali Baba; it is known for its carved wood architecture.

kalemegdan.fait: This park, the largest in Belgrade, overlooks the confluence of the Sava and the Danube and contains the city's old fortress.

marche-ljubljana.fait: This covered market on the banks of the Ljubljanica was designed by the architect Jože Plečnik; it is sometimes called Plečnik's Market.

mosquee-plomb.fait: This 18th-century Ottoman mosque in Shkodër is named after the lead that covers its domes.

tetes-noires.fait: This famous medieval house in Riga is called Melngalvju nams in Latvian and Schwarzhäupterhaus in German.

palais-recteurs.fait: This Dubrovnik palace housed the seat of the rector of the Republic of Ragusa, as well as an armory, powder magazines and a prison.

lovrijenac.fait: According to legend, this Dubrovnik fort was built in just three months to beat the Venetians, who wanted to control the city.

saint-domnius.fait: This Catholic cathedral, dedicated to Domnius of Salona, stands inside Diocletian's Palace itself, in Split.

baba-vida.fait: Built on a hill in Vidin, on the banks of the Danube, this fortress is one of the few Bulgarian fortresses dating from the 10th century.

vieux-rauma.fait: This historic center of the town of Rauma is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; in Swedish, it is called Gamla Raumo.

hame.fait: This medieval castle is called Hämeen linna in Finnish, almost like the town of Hämeenlinna where it stands.

cathedrale-turku.fait: Built over a very long period, this Turku cathedral blends Romanesque, Gothic and Gothic Revival styles; it is the only medieval basilica in Finland.

seurasaari.fait: This Helsinki island, connected by a bridge, has no permanent residents; on about a third of its area, an open-air museum brings together old wooden buildings.

tour-ronde.fait: This Copenhagen tower is part of a complex built to offer scholars an astronomical observatory, a church and a library all at once.

eglise-marbre.fait: It is called the “Marble Church,” but this Copenhagen church officially has another name: Frederik's Church.

bakken.fait: This amusement park grew up around a spring discovered in the forest: the walkers it attracted gradually drew in street performers and attractions.

hraunfossar.fait: Their Icelandic name means “the lava falls”: they are a series of small waterfalls in western Iceland, near Reykholt.

dohany.fait: With 3,500 seats, this Budapest synagogue is considered the largest in Europe, by its capacity rather than by its size.

galdhopiggen.fait: This mountain in Jotunheimen is the highest peak in Norway, but also in the whole Scandinavian Peninsula and Northern Europe.

lysefjord.fait: Its name means “fjord of light”: it is said to come from the granite that colors its walls, carved out by glaciers.

hommage-prussien.fait: In this painting, Jan Matejko depicted over thirty figures of the Polish Renaissance, several of whom were absent that day.

grue-gdansk.fait: This harbor crane, which also serves as a water gate, is the largest and oldest medieval port crane in Europe.

ogrodzieniec.fait: This 14th-century castle, enlarged many times, has remained in ruins since it was devastated during the Great Northern War.

biskupin.fait: A schoolteacher found this fortified settlement while out for a walk: he had seen wooden stakes and pieces of pottery emerging from a lake.

jasna-gora.fait: According to tradition, the Black Madonna kept in this shrine was painted by Saint Luke on the table of the Holy Family.

sauveur-sang.nom: Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood
sauveur-sang.fait: The “spilled blood” in its name is that of Emperor Alexander II, who was mortally wounded on the very spot where the church was built.

cavalier-bronze.fait: This statue of Peter the Great, commissioned by Catherine II from the Frenchman Falconet, rests on one of the largest stones ever moved by humans.

vallee-geysers.fait: These geysers in Kamchatka are accessible almost only by helicopter, and visiting permits there are limited to 48 hours.

manpupuner.fait: These seven rock columns in the Urals, sculpted by wind and ice, bear a Mansi name meaning “small mountain of the Gods.”

metro-moscou.fait: This metro, with its often deep stations and carefully crafted decor, never stopped its extension works, even during the Second World War.

pierre-et-paul.fait: Saint Petersburg was founded here, and the fortress cathedral holds the tombs of all the Russian emperors since Peter the Great.

fermes-halsingland.fait: Having grown wealthy, the farmers of this region brought in local artists or artists from Dalarna to decorate their homes, especially their large reception rooms.

kebnekaise.fait: Its Sami name means “cauldron rim”: despite its remote region, this highest point in Sweden is a popular hiking destination.

lorette-prague.fait: This pilgrimage shrine in Prague houses a copy of the Holy House of Loreto and a bell tower with a famous carillon.

oreilles-stramberk.fait: These gingerbread cones may bear their name only if they are made in Štramberk: even their shape is protected by the European Union.

akkerman.fait: In Moldovan as in Turkish, its names mean “white citadel”: this medieval town girded by ramparts stood at the mouth of the Dniester.

fourah-bay.fait: Located in Freetown, this university is the main institution of higher education in Sierra Leone.

badiar.fait: This park adjoins Senegal’s Niokolo-Koba: visitors can move freely from one to the other, but they mostly stay on the Senegalese side, which has more hotels.

moukalaba.fait: Between forest and coastline, this park in southwestern Gabon is said to have one of the highest densities of primates in the country.

transgabonais.fait: Gabon’s only railway line is used mainly to transport logs and manganese, and it still operates at a loss.

ilheu-cabras.fait: Its name means “goat islet”: it is one of the smallest islands in the archipelago, northeast of São Tomé, and people go diving and kayaking there.

kaouar.fait: Thanks to their springs, the oases along this escarpment were a stop on the trans-Saharan trade routes; in the Middle Ages, dates and salt were produced there.

turkana-parcs.fait: These three parks lie on the saltiest of the great African lakes; at Koobi Fora, fossil deposits shed light on the continent’s ancient landscapes.

meru.fait: It was here that George and Joy Adamson released the son of Elsa the lioness, heroine of the book Born Free, as well as their cheetah Pippa.

shimba-hills.fait: This small coastal reserve is home to more than half of Kenya’s rare plant species, including endangered cycads and orchids.

usambara.fait: In their eastern range, the one closest to the Indian Ocean, these mountains bear a tropical rainforest, a rather unusual case in East Africa.

chumbe.fait: This small coral island in the Zanzibar Channel is a private nature reserve, known for its “ecological innovation” and its reefs.

isimangaliso.fait: According to Nelson Mandela, it is probably the only place where rhinoceros, elephant, coelacanth and whale share the same ecosystem.

vredefort.fait: This dome is the largest known impact crater on Earth, and the town of Vredefort was built right inside the crater.

betsiboka.fait: This river in the north of the island gave its name to a region; its main tributary, the Ikopa, flows through the capital, Antananarivo.

baobab-grandidier.fait: This tree is endemic to Madagascar: in the wild, it grows nowhere else in the world.

pervenche.fait: This flower contains vincristine and vinblastine, molecules used in chemotherapy against many cancers.

palmier-arec.fait: Native to Madagascar, this palm is sold as an “air-purifying” plant, but in a real room the effect is negligible: you would need hundreds of pots.

ras-dashen.fait: This summit, the highest in Ethiopia, presents no climbing difficulty; a Westerner first climbed it in 1841.

omo.fait: This river’s floods are essential to local crops, and its lower valley has yielded hominin fossils, some of them several million years old.

awash.fait: This park brings together very different landscapes: the Awash canyon and its falls, the Fentale volcano and its fumaroles, and hot springs.

lac-kainji.fait: This lake was created by a dam on the Niger River; the national park surrounding it is the oldest in Nigeria.

lac-guiers.fait: Less famous than the Pink Lake, this freshwater lake in the north of the country is nonetheless the largest in Senegal.

fadiouth.fait: This village is an artificial island made of piled-up shells, connected to the coast by a wooden bridge.

lobeke.fait: This equatorial forest park is grouped with a Central African reserve and a Congolese park in the Sangha Trinational, a joint conservation initiative.

delta-niger.fait: Here, the Niger River splits into many branches before joining up again: it is the largest wetland in all of West Africa.

santa-luzia.fait: With no trees or water, this island in the north of the Cape Verde archipelago is now uninhabited.

semuliki.fait: This park protects East Africa’s only lowland tropical forest, one of the richest areas of the continent in biodiversity, especially birds.

nyamuragira.fait: This volcano, the most active in Africa, can produce lava flows long enough to reach Lake Kivu, located to the south.

lofoi.fait: These falls, the highest in Central Africa, carry so little water that in the dry season it vanishes into the air.

ile-mozambique.fait: This island gave its name to the coast facing it and to the entire country, after Sultan Mussa Mbiki, who ruled it when Vasco da Gama arrived.

kouilou.fait: This river changes its name along the way: it is called the Niari upstream of the Sounda gorges, then the Kouilou in the coastal region.

cathedrale-asmara.fait: Wrongly called a “cathedral,” this church in Asmara has a bell tower loosely inspired by the tower of the Palace of Westminster in London.

likoma-ile.fait: Although surrounded by Mozambican waters, this island in Lake Malawi belongs to Malawi, a legacy of the 19th-century Anglican missionaries.

zambezi-np.fait: This park upstream of Victoria Falls is cut in two by a road: one side borders the Zambezi, the other runs along the Chamabonda vlei.

fachi.fait: Also called Agram, this oasis is surrounded by the Ténéré desert and by the dunes of the Erg of Bilma.

mare-hippopotames.fait: This classified forest, home to about sixty hippopotamuses, is managed by a villagers’ association.

ile-rusinga.fait: This volcanic island in Lake Victoria, rich in prehistoric fossils, is connected to the mainland by a narrow artificial causeway.

koobi-fora.fait: This site on Lake Turkana yields fossils of the earliest Hominini; its name means “the place where Commiphora grow” in the Gabbra language.

chateau-bonne-esperance.fait: This star fort was built on the former shoreline of Table Bay; today it stands in the center of Cape Town, on land reclaimed from the sea.

big-hole.fait: This former open-pit mine, dug into a kimberlite pipe, contained one of the richest diamond deposits ever discovered.

cap-aiguilles.fait: This cape, called Cabo das Agulhas in Portuguese, is the southernmost point of the entire African continent.

richtersveld.fait: The Nama have lived in these mountainous deserts for 2,000 years, in portable houses covered with rush mats.

blombos.fait: The oldest known drawing in the world was found in this cave: nine crisscrossing lines traced on a small pebble.

disa-uniflora.fait: This South African orchid is the type species of its genus; it is sometimes still referred to by its old name, Disa grandiflora.

tsimanampetsotsa.fait: This park in Toliara Province, one of Madagascar’s first Ramsar sites, has been a World Heritage Site since 2023, together with the dry forests of Andrefana.

mangoky.fait: The longest river on the western side of Madagascar, it flows into the Mozambique Channel through a vast delta.

tahina.fait: Nicknamed the “suicide palm,” this rare palm bears the first name of its discoverers’ daughter, which means “blessed” in Malagasy.

baobab-fony.fait: Typical of Madagascar’s dry forests, this tree stores water in its trunk, which resembles that of a small baobab.

nechisar.fait: Its name means “white grass”; the park is home to the “Bridge of God,” an isthmus between Lake Abaya and Lake Chamo.

gashaka-gumti.fait: Created by merging two game reserves, this park has become the largest national park in Nigeria.

casamance-fleuve.fait: This river owes its name to the Kasa Mansa, king of the precolonial kingdom of Kasa, and crosses Casamance from east to west to the Atlantic.

mont-oku.fait: This summit in the Northwest Region is a volcano, one of those that make up the Cameroon Line.

rodrigues.fait: Nicknamed “the Cinderella of the Mascarenes,” this island has a lagoon twice as large as its land area.

brandberg.fait: This massif bears Namibia’s highest point, the Königstein, and is home to a great many rock painting sites.

namib-naukluft.fait: This park, straddling the Namib Desert and the Naukluft Mountains, is home to Sossusvlei, Namibia’s main tourist site.

bwabwata.fait: Unusually, about 5,500 people live in this park, and they take part in managing it together with their neighbors.

mikeno.fait: Its name means “poor,” so harsh and uninhabitable are its slopes; yet they are home to some of the last mountain gorillas.

reserve-maputo.fait: Formerly called the Maputo Elephant Reserve, this reserve is now part of transfrontier conservation areas.

bahr-el-ghazal.fait: Its Arabic name means “river of the gazelles”; this river joins the Nile by way of the White Nile.

pate.fait: On this small island of the Lamu Archipelago, in the Indian Ocean, no motor vehicles are in use.

manda-ke.fait: Prosperous in the 9th century, its towns were probably abandoned for lack of water; today the island has almost no permanent residents.

pangani.fait: This river in the northeast of the country rises in a reservoir, Nyumba ya Mungu, then flows into the Indian Ocean.

awash-river.fait: This river flows north through the Great Rift Valley to Lake Abbe, and its lower valley yielded the fossils of the australopithecine Lucy.

tugela-river.fait: The largest river in the province of KwaZulu-Natal, it crosses the province before flowing into the Indian Ocean.

vaal.fait: Its name means “dull”: it refers to the color of its waters, especially in the flood season, when the river is laden with silt.

great-fish.fait: Called the Groot-Visrivier in Afrikaans, this river crosses the Eastern Cape and reaches the Indian Ocean between Port Elizabeth and East London.

swakop.fait: Though usually dry, this river has made it possible to develop agriculture in the Swakopmund area, known for its asparagus, olives and tomatoes.

boteti.fait: This river in Botswana, which has no outlet to the sea, rises in the very heart of the Okavango Delta.

chambeshi.fait: Pronounced “chambezi,” this river in northeastern Zambia joins the Luapula and thus feeds the Congo River.

cuvo.fait: Called the Cuvo in its upper course, this river changes its name downstream, where it is known as the Keve or Queve.

catumbela.fait: This coastal river rises in the Cassoco hills and flows into the Atlantic between Lobito and Benguela.

ngounie.fait: This river gives its name to a Gabonese province; it flows through Mouila before joining the Ogooué upstream of Lambaréné.

oueme.fait: It is the most important river in Benin, leaving aside the Niger, which merely marks the country’s border.

zou.fait: This river in western Benin, which flows into the Ouémé, gave its name to an entire department of the country.

nyabarongo.fait: This river in Rwanda, part of the Nile basin, is born from the meeting of two streams, the Mbirurume and the Mwogo.

lac-iro.fait: This almost circular lake in Chad, fed by the Bahr Salamat, is suspected of occupying a meteorite impact crater.

erg-bilma.fait: This sea of dunes in the Ténéré, in the southern Sahara, surrounds the oasis of Bilma on three sides, near the border with Chad.

tenakourou.fait: This highest point of Burkina Faso was almost as high as a neighboring summit in Mali: stones were piled on it to widen the gap.

lagdo.fait: This lake is not natural: it formed behind a dam on the Benue, in northern Cameroon, and its waters join the Niger basin.

ankobra.fait: This river in Ghana rises near Wiawso and then runs due south until it flows into the Gulf of Guinea.

three-points.fait: This small peninsula in Ghana marks the western limit of the Bight of Benin; together with Cape Lopez, in Gabon, it bounds the inner Gulf of Guinea.

ogun-river.fait: This coastal river crosses three Nigerian states, Oyo, Ogun and Lagos, before ending in the Lagos Lagoon, which is connected to the Bight of Benin.

mambilla.fait: This plateau in Taraba State, in eastern Nigeria, runs along the border with Cameroon; its name is also spelled Mambila.

ilheu-branco.fait: This uninhabited islet in northern Cape Verde nestles between the island of Santa Luzia and Raso, another islet barely larger than it.

praslin.fait: This island in the Seychelles is home to the Vallée de Mai, a reserve rich in endemic species, in particular five species of palm.

aride.fait: This island, the northernmost of the Seychelles’ granitic islands, has only six inhabitants, housed in small houses on the south coast.

felicite.fait: Until the 1970s, this island in the Seychelles had a coconut plantation; it is now home to a luxury resort.

desroches.fait: This island in the Amirantes group, in the Seychelles, is a private island with a luxury hotel.

alphonse.fait: This atoll in the Seychelles has only one island, where 300 people live alongside a tourist hotel and a small airport.

farquhar.fait: This atoll of the Farquhar Group, in the Outer Islands of the Seychelles, is recognized as an Important Bird Area.

agalega.fait: This coral archipelago, a remote territory of Mauritius, consists of two islands, North Island and South Island, connected by a sandy isthmus.

ile-monos.fait: This island owes its name to the red howler monkeys that once lived there: “monos” means monkeys in Spanish.

pic-blue-mountain.fait: This summit is the highest point in all of Jamaica; it lies in the Blue Mountains range.

goldeneye-fleming.fait: In this house, where he spent every winter, Ian Fleming wrote the adventures of James Bond; today it is part of a hotel.

new-providence.fait: This island is home to more than 60% of the population of the Bahamas; a governor is said to have named it “Providence” to thank heaven after a shipwreck.

inagua.fait: This district includes two islands, Great Inagua and Little Inagua; its main town, Matthew Town, has only about five hundred inhabitants.

ozama.fait: It was on the west bank of this river’s mouth that Santo Domingo, the country’s capital, developed from the end of the 15th century.

lac-de-peligre.fait: This lake in the Centre department is the second-largest lake in Haiti, just after Étang Saumâtre.

patuca.fait: Born from the meeting of the Guayape and the Guayambre, this river is the longest in Honduras and the second-largest in Central America.

parc-jeannette-kawas.fait: Originally called Punta Sal National Park, this park is managed by the very foundation that created it; it is also designated a Ramsar site.

ile-conchaguita.fait: In 1892, an earthquake there triggered a landslide whose dust cloud was at first mistaken for ash from an eruption.

taburete.fait: This volcano in El Salvador is topped by a well-preserved crater; its highest point is on the southern rim of this crater.

coupe-gaillard.fait: This artificial valley was cut through Panama for the canal; its excavation was one of the greatest civil engineering challenges of its time.

ile-taboga.fait: Nicknamed the “island of flowers,” this volcanic island in the Gulf of Panama lies off the Pacific entrance to the canal.

cathedrale-sainte-marie-pa.fait: Begun in 1688, this cathedral in the old town of Panama City was not consecrated until 1796, 108 years later.

lac-alajuela.fait: This artificial lake serves as a reservoir for the Panama Canal; one day, its record level forced the canal to close for 17 hours.

escudo-de-veraguas.fait: Cut off from the mainland only 9,000 years ago, this island is home to two endemic mammals, including a pygmy sloth, both threatened with extinction.

peninsule-nicoya.fait: This peninsula on the Pacific coast of Costa Rica is divided between two provinces: Guanacaste to the north and Puntarenas to the south.

volcan-barva.fait: This volcano in the Central Cordillera, 2,906 meters high, is also known as Barba and Las Tres Marías.

tarcoles.fait: This river’s basin is home to about half the population of Costa Rica, and its banks are frequented by the American crocodile.

parc-carara.fait: This park protects the basin of the Tárcoles River and is home to one of the country’s last large populations of wild scarlet macaws.

cascade-la-paz.fait: Formed by the successive drops of the La Paz River, this waterfall was severely affected by an earthquake in 2009.

cascade-la-fortuna.fait: The name of this waterfall in the province of Alajuela, in central Costa Rica, means “fortune” in Spanish.

tajumulco.fait: This volcano, the highest point in all of Central America, remains little known because of its isolation, even though climbing it presents no difficulty.

volcan-atitlan.fait: This volcano bordering Lake Atitlán has had more than a dozen recorded eruptions; the last one dates back to 1853.

nakbe.fait: Ceramics decorated with the woven mat, a symbol of power, were found there: this power was therefore already in place in the Preclassic period.

volcan-san-pedro-gt.fait: This volcano, about 3,020 meters high, is, along with Tolimán and Atitlán, one of the three volcanoes bordering the south of Lake Atitlán.

cancuen.fait: The name of this city means “place of the serpent” in ancient Maya; it was probably one of the most important trading centers of the Maya world.

naranjo-maya.fait: In the Classic period, this Maya city is thought to have been called Saal; it formed alliances with several cities that were enemies of Tikal.

san-bartolo-maya.fait: A mural of the maize god was discovered there: it shows that this kind of painting existed 300 years before the Classic period.

torre-del-reformador.fait: This steel tower in Guatemala City resembles the Eiffel Tower; the bell placed at its top has been replaced by a beacon.

laguna-lachua.fait: The slightly sulfurous smell of this lake is thought to explain its name, taken from the Q’eqchi’ “la chu ha,” which means “fetid water.”

nakum.fait: Apart from Tikal, this site is the Classic Maya site with the largest number of inscriptions in Maya script.

topoxte.fait: This Postclassic Maya site in Petén was the capital of the northern quarter of the Itza kingdom, that of the Ko’woj clan, also called Couoch.

temple-grand-jaguar.fait: This pyramid in Tikal has 9 tiers, a sacred Maya number, and hides a burial chamber dedicated to the ruler who had it built.

cathedrale-saint-jacques-gt.fait: Blending Baroque and Neoclassical styles, the massive structure of this cathedral has survived many earthquakes; its towers were completed in 1867.

qumarkaj.fait: Capital of the K’iche’ Maya when the Spanish arrived, this city was later looted: its stones were used to build the nearby town of Santa Cruz del Quiché.

fort-el-morro.fait: This fort guarding the entrance to Havana Bay owes its full name to the three Magi of the Bible.

forteresse-cabana.fait: Built by Spain at the entrance to the port of Havana, this fortress became a prison where Che Guevara set up his headquarters in 1959.

plantations-cafe-sud-est.nom: First Coffee Plantations of the South-East
plantations-cafe-sud-est.fait: These remains in the Sierra Maestra bear witness to a way of exploiting virgin forest for coffee whose traces have disappeared elsewhere in the world.

guitarron.fait: This plucked string instrument looks like a large guitar; born in the late 19th century, it is often confused with the bajo sexto.

calavera.fait: These skulls of the Day of the Dead were promoted in the 1920s by governments to unify Mexico after the revolution.

escamoles.fait: This “Mexican caviar” is made of ant pupae, small balls that are sometimes wrongly called “ant eggs.”

cenote-ik-kil.fait: This cenote near Chichén Itzá, nicknamed the “sacred blue cenote,” is open to the public and even hosts diving competitions.

canyon-du-sumidero.fait: This canyon in Chiapas was carved by the Grijalva River, which then runs on to the Gulf of Mexico; it is part of a national park.

bonampak.fait: The rediscovery of this small Maya site was long credited to a man who came to shoot a documentary there; we now know that others had preceded him.

cacaxtla.fait: This site is famous for its many murals; its name is thought to come from the Nahuatl “cacaxtli,” a wooden frame for carrying goods.

dzibilchaltun.fait: At the spring equinox, the rising sun shines straight through one window of the Temple of the Seven Dolls and comes out through the opposite window.

labna.fait: Like the other cities of the Puuc region, these Maya ruins are well known to archaeologists, but their history remains much more obscure.

edzna.fait: This site has one of the rare examples in the Yucatán of a Maya pyramid whose tiers are fitted with vaulted chambers.

tonina.fait: This medium-sized Maya city nevertheless sacked its rival Palenque; its Tzeltal name means “Great House of Stone.”

san-juan-de-ulua.fait: This small island, now enclosed within the port of Veracruz, was discovered in 1518 by the Spaniard Juan de Grijalva; it is best known for its fortress.

ile-guadalupe-mx.fait: This volcanic island in the Pacific, off Baja California, is the westernmost point of Mexican territory.

lac-de-chapala.fait: This lake is the largest in Mexico, but it is so shallow that it does not constitute a large freshwater reserve.

janitzio.fait: The name of this island in Lake Pátzcuaro means “corn flower” in Purépecha; its town is perched on top of a hill.

bibliotheque-palafoxiana.fait: Founded as early as 1646 in Puebla, this library is the oldest in the Americas; its collection was digitized during its restoration after an earthquake.

peintures-sierra-san-francisco.nom: Rock Paintings of the Sierra de San Francisco
peintures-sierra-san-francisco.fait: Hidden in caves in Baja California, these paintings are considered one of the finest collections of rock art in the world.

lac-peyto.fait: This lake in the Rockies, in Banff National Park in Alberta, is easily reached from the Icefields Parkway.

parc-yoho.fait: This park in the Rockies, the smallest of four neighboring parks, is home to the Burgess Shale, which is particularly rich in fossils.

parc-kootenay.fait: The Rocky Mountain goat is the emblem of this park, which takes its name from the Kootenay River, one of the rivers that flow through it.

ile-du-cap-breton.fait: Once called Île Royale, this Nova Scotia island is famous for its fiddle music of Scottish origin and the French fortress of Louisbourg.

chateau-laurier.fait: Close to Parliament Hill, this Ottawa hotel has housed and brought together several notable politicians, hence its nickname “the third chamber of Parliament.”

banff-springs.fait: This hotel, right in the middle of Banff National Park, was built in the “Château” style by the architect Bruce Price.

pont-de-quebec.fait: After disastrous construction work, this bridge over the St. Lawrence became the cantilever bridge with the longest clear span in the world.

grand-pre.fait: Founded in 1682, this village quickly became the breadbasket and main town of Acadia; its landscape has been a World Heritage Site since 2012.

mont-logan.fait: This summit, the highest point in Canada, endures an average of 300 days of bad weather a year, with polar temperatures.

lac-maligne.fait: This lake in Jasper is famous for the color of its waters and for Spirit Island; its trout, on the other hand, were introduced by humans.

iles-de-la-madeleine.fait: Jacques Cartier first named these islands “Araynes,” from the Latin arena, sand; six of them are linked by sandbars.

schistes-de-burgess.fait: The fossils of this deposit in the Rockies have kept their appendages and soft parts, which are very rarely preserved.

miguasha.fait: Thousands of fossils have been collected from the cliff of this Quebec park, created specifically to protect the fossil site.

jardins-butchart.fait: These floral display gardens on Vancouver Island receive more than a million visitors every year.

parc-algonquin.fait: This Ontario park, the first provincial park in Canada, contains more than 2,400 lakes, on the boundary between coniferous and deciduous forests.

mont-thor.fait: The face of this mountain on Baffin Island, which leans at an average angle of 105 degrees, was used to set the world record for the longest rappel.

pingualuit.fait: This crater in Nunavik, formed by a meteorite, is the smallest of the eight impact structures recognized in Quebec.

basilique-sainte-anne-de-beaupre.fait: This shrine, considered one of the main pilgrimage sites in North America, holds relics of Saint Anne, mother of the Virgin Mary.

green-gables.fait: This farm on Prince Edward Island inspired Lucy Maud Montgomery to write the novel “Anne of Green Gables.”

yuna.fait: This river, one of the three main rivers of the Dominican Republic, rises near Bonao and flows into Samaná Bay.

rio-bayano.fait: This river in eastern Panama has two names, Río Bayano or Río Chepo, and flows through the Kuna comarca of Madugandí.

lac-bayano.fait: This lake did not exist before 1976: it was created by the construction of the Bayano Dam on the Bayano River, in the east of Panamá Province.

lac-chicabal.fait: A sacred place of the Mam Maya, this crater lake is closed to swimming, and altars on its shores are still used for ceremonies.

lac-d-ipala.fait: This lake sits in the main crater of the Ipala volcano, at an altitude of 1,493 meters, in the southeast of the department of Chiquimula.

petexbatun.fait: Around this lake, Maya cities abandoned during the collapse of their civilization have helped archaeologists explain it better.

naj-tunich.fait: The discovery of this cave, which is also a Maya site, played a pioneering role in the archaeology of that civilization's caves.

cuicuilco.fait: This city, perhaps the oldest in the Valley of Mexico, was destroyed and abandoned after the eruption of the Xitle volcano.

becan.fait: This Maya site was surrounded by an oval defensive system, a ditch backed by an embankment, pierced by seven passageways.

sayil.fait: With no rivers and a porous subsoil, this Maya city had a large number of chultuns, underground cisterns.

iles-revillagigedo.fait: These volcanic islands lie at the heart of a marine reserve regarded as North America's equivalent of the Galapagos Islands.

iles-marietas.fait: This uninhabited archipelago, a former military zone, is known for its artificial beach created by the explosion of a bomb.

comalcalco.fait: This site resembles the other Maya cities of the Classic period, with one difference: its large buildings are made of brick.

cabo-pulmo.fait: Its waters are home to the only living hard coral reef in North America; Commander Cousteau saw it as “the aquarium of the world.”

chutes-athabasca.fait: These falls are impressive less for their height than for their power, due to the large quantity of water pouring into the gorge.

ile-d-orleans.fait: Many Quebecers and Franco-Americans descend from the first inhabitants of this island, one of the first places settled in New France.

monts-torngat.fait: The highest point of this range has two names: Mont D'Iberville on the Quebec side, Mount Caubvik on the Newfoundland and Labrador side.

ile-de-baffin.fait: This island, the largest in Canada, is slightly bigger than Spain; in Old Norse it was called Helluland, “land of the flat stone.”

pointe-pelee.fait: This park is the southernmost mainland in Canada, at the same latitude as northern California.

parc-forillon.fait: This park on the Gaspé Peninsula marks the northern end of the Quebec Appalachians, among forests, cliffs, dunes, and salt marshes.

hotel-du-parlement-qc.fait: This building houses the National Assembly of Quebec, but the square in front of its central door is federal property.

musique-soul.fait: This African American music, born in the late 1950s, draws on both church gospel and rhythm and blues.

venus-willendorf.fait: This Paleolithic limestone figurine was discovered in 1908 during construction work on a railroad line.

baiser-klimt.fait: This painting is done on a canvas covered with gold leaf, and its models are probably Klimt himself and his companion.

couronne-rodolphe.fait: Made in Prague as the personal crown of Emperor Rudolf II, it later became the official crown of the Austrian Empire.

belvedere-vienne.fait: It was in this Baroque palace in Vienna that the treaty by which Austria regained its independence after World War II was signed.

burgtheater.fait: Founded in 1741, this Vienna theater is the second oldest in Europe, just after the Comédie-Française.

cathedrale-salzbourg.fait: It was in this 17th-century Baroque cathedral, dedicated to Saint Rupert, that Mozart was baptized.

votivkirche.fait: This neo-Gothic Catholic church was built in the mid-19th century on the Ring, Vienna's circular boulevard.

hellbrunn.fait: Part of the large landscaped area onto which the garden of this palace opens, south of Salzburg, is now occupied by the city zoo.

klosterneuburg.fait: Located north of Vienna, in Lower Austria, this abbey is home to a community of Augustinian canons.

vierge-van-der-paele.nom: Virgin and Child with Canon van der Paele
vierge-van-der-paele.fait: This painting by Van Eyck was meant to serve as an epitaph for the canon who commissioned it, in the Bruges church where he would be buried.

herve.fait: It is the only cheese in Belgium protected by a European designation of origin; it is described as “spicy” or “mild.”

denombrement-bethleem.fait: This painting by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, painted in 1566, is kept in Brussels at the Oldmasters Museum.

procession-saint-sang.fait: Dating from the Middle Ages, this large religious procession takes place every year in Bruges on Ascension Day.

chasse-ursule.fait: The paintings with which Hans Memling decorated the four sides and the roof of this Bruges reliquary tell the story of Saint Ursula.

musee-plantin-moretus.fait: This Antwerp museum is devoted to a 16th-century printing house, founded by Christophe Plantin and later run by his descendants.

cathedrale-saints-michel-gudule.nom: Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula
cathedrale-saints-michel-gudule.fait: This Gothic cathedral in Brussels is dedicated to Saint Michael and Saint Gudula, the two patron saints of the city.

ascenseurs-canal-centre.nom: Boat Lifts on the Canal du Centre
ascenseurs-canal-centre.fait: On this canal in Hainaut, it is hydraulic lifts, built from 1888 onward, that raise and lower the boats.

hotel-ville-bruxelles.fait: This Gothic building is the only medieval survivor on the Grand-Place of Brussels, where it faces the King's House.

palais-justice-bruxelles.fait: This palace has been under construction work for so long that some of the scaffolding put up for its renovation has itself had to be renovated.

beffroi-gand.fait: Charles V had the first Roland bell of this belfry cracked, so that its hoarse ringing would remind the inhabitants of a punishment.

chateau-habsbourg.fait: This castle in Aargau belonged to the Habsburgs, the family that ruled Austria, Spain and, in the Middle Ages, a good part of Switzerland.

glacier-rhone.fait: This glacier in Valais is the source of the Rhône, and a tunnel dug into the ice allows visitors to see its interior.

titlis.fait: This very accessible peak in Central Switzerland offers a panorama of the Bernese Alps and Lake Lucerne.

santis.fait: This peak, the highest in the Alpstein massif, is shared by three cantons: the two Appenzells and St. Gallen.

grossmunster.fait: The theology school of this Zurich church, a center of the Reformation under Zwingli, gave rise to the city's university.

rigi.fait: Humanists believed its name came from the Latin for “queen of the mountains”; it actually comes from an Alemannic word meaning “band.”

chateaux-bellinzone.fait: These castles and their wall controlled a crossroads of Alpine routes; a Roman fort already occupied the rock in the 4th century.

cathedrale-lausanne.fait: Since 1405, a watchman has kept watch in the belfry of this cathedral, and he still calls out the hours from there.

fraumunster.fait: This church in the heart of Zurich is famous for its stained-glass windows by Marc Chagall and Augusto Giacometti.

creux-du-van.fait: This rocky cirque in the Neuchâtel Jura lies at the heart of a nature reserve; the top of its cliff partly marks the border with Vaud.

munot.fait: This fortress overlooks the old town of Schaffhausen, of whose power it was long the symbol.

chateau-tarasp.fait: Perched on a rocky hill in the Lower Engadine, this castle is the emblem of Tarasp, a former municipality now part of Scuol.

bible-gutenberg.fait: Printed in Mainz in the 15th century, it is the first book in Europe set with movable type.

voyageur-mer-nuages.nom: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
voyageur-mer-nuages.fait: Painted by Caspar David Friedrich starting in 1818, this work of German Romanticism is on display at the Hamburger Kunsthalle.

disque-nebra.fait: Dug up by illegal treasure hunters, this bronze and gold disc is considered the oldest known depiction of the sky.

homme-lion.fait: Carved from mammoth ivory, this figure of a cave lion stands upright, which gives it a human appearance.

porcelaine-meissen.fait: Pieces from the Meissen manufactory, made with kaolin from the nearby mines, can be recognized by two crossed swords.

kieler-woche.fait: This sailing competition in Kiel is accompanied by a gathering of tall ships and one of the largest public festivals in Europe.

gose.fait: This beer contains salt and coriander; it takes its name from the Gose, a small river that flows through Goslar.

prinzregententorte.fait: In Munich, this chocolate cake made of thin layers of sponge cake is as popular as the Sachertorte in Vienna.

printen.fait: This specialty of Aachen, made of flour, sugar, brown sugar and spices, has a protected designation of origin.

feuerzangenbowle.fait: A rum-soaked sugarloaf is set alight above mulled wine: it is a traditional drink for Christmas and New Year's Eve.

handkase.fait: Topped with chopped onions, this small hand-shaped cheese from Hesse becomes “Handkäse mit Musik,” “Handkäse with music.”

osterbrunnen.fait: At Easter, villages in Bavaria decorate their public fountains with painted eggs and flowers.

cathedrale-spire.fait: This cathedral, the largest Romanesque one in the world, served as the burial place of eight German emperors and kings.

nymphenburg.fait: Once the summer residence of the rulers of Bavaria, this Munich palace is even wider than the Palace of Versailles.

residence-wurtzbourg.fait: This Baroque palace was the home of the prince-bishops of Würzburg; it is compared to Schönbrunn Palace or to Versailles.

wieskirche.fait: Dedicated to the Scourged Savior, this Rococo pilgrimage church stands amid forests, peat bogs and meadows.

brocken.fait: This mountain in Saxony-Anhalt is the highest point of the Harz, in northern Germany, and is part of Harz National Park.

cathedrale-bamberg.fait: Completed in the 13th century, this UNESCO-listed cathedral is the seat of the Catholic Archdiocese of Bamberg.

herrenchiemsee.fait: This copy of Versailles on an island is also called “Meicost Ettal,” an anagram of “L'État, c'est moi.”

chilehaus.fait: This “Chile House” is an office building in Hamburg, one of the first examples of brick Expressionist architecture.

externsteine.fait: The name of these rocks in Westphalia is a corruption of “Eckensternensteine,” the “stones with starry corners.”

menines.fait: At the back of this painting, a mirror reflects the king and queen, as if they were standing in the place of the person looking at the canvas.

fileuses.fait: The true title of this painting by Velázquez is The Fable of Arachne; it has remained relatively little known compared with the success of Las Meninas.

famille-charles-iv.fait: Goya drew inspiration from Velázquez's Las Meninas for this portrait of King Charles IV surrounded by his family.

barretina.fait: This long wool cap, often red, is the traditional headwear of Catalan men; women wear a gandalla.

maja-vetue.fait: Painted by Goya around 1800, this canvas was long exhibited at the Royal Academy of San Fernando before joining the Prado.

cabrales.fait: This blue cheese from Asturias can blend cow's, sheep's and goat's milk in a single cheese.

patxaran.fait: This liqueur from Navarre is made of wild sloes steeped in anise-flavored alcohol; its name comes from Basque.

dame-elche.fait: This stone bust of a woman, discovered near Elche in 1897, is the best-known relic of Iberian culture.

idiazabal.fait: This Basque and Navarrese cheese is made from raw milk of Latxa and Carranzana sheep, and ripens for at least two months.

marmitako.fait: This stew of tuna with potatoes, onions, peppers and tomatoes was born among Basque and Cantabrian fishermen.

queimada.fait: An incantation is recited while preparing this Galician punch, which is then set alight: it is supposed to grant powers to those who drink it.

leche-frita.fait: This “fried milk” is a dough of flour, milk and sugar that is cut into portions once it has thickened, then fried.

timple.fait: This small guitar from the Canary Islands is thought to derive from the Baroque guitar, brought by the Spanish during the conquest of the islands.

fideua.fait: This culinary specialty of the Valencian region bears in Catalan the name “fideu,” which means “vermicelli.”

cathedrale-burgos.fait: Its many works of art make this Castilian cathedral a museum of European Gothic sculpture.

generalife.fait: This summer palace of the Nasrid princes of Granada is cooled by pools fed by springs from the Sierra Nevada.

palais-musique-catalane.fait: This Barcelona concert hall was paid for by patrons to serve as the home of a choral society, the Orfeó Català.

medulas.fait: This landscape of reddish sands was profoundly transformed by the Romans, who mined gold there.

bardenas.fait: This semi-desert in Navarre, sculpted by erosion, served as a setting for scenes in the series Game of Thrones.

torre-del-oro.fait: Built by the Almohads in the 13th century, this military tower guarded access to Seville via the Guadalquivir.

parc-retiro.fait: Created in the 17th century, this large park in the city of Madrid is now home to more than 15,000 trees.

penseur.fait: This sculpture by Rodin was first called The Poet and was originally just one element of The Gates of Hell.

impression-soleil-levant.fait: The title of this painting by Monet, exhibited in 1874, gave its name to an entire movement in painting: Impressionism.

dejeuner-herbe.fait: A naked woman looking at the viewer, beside two fully dressed men: this painting by Manet caused a scandal in 1863.

bal-moulin-galette.nom: Bal du moulin de la Galette
bal-moulin-galette.fait: In this painting, Renoir depicts a dance in Montmartre in light filtered through the leaves; the State received it in 1894 as a bequest from Caillebotte.

bourgeois-calais.fait: Rodin turned a banal medieval surrender ritual into an act of heroism: six burghers giving themselves up to save their city.

cantal.fait: It takes 400 liters of milk to make a single wheel of this cheese, which is named after the mountains it comes from.

epoisses.fait: This washed-rind cheese from Burgundy is named after the village of Époisses; its best season for eating runs from May to October.

glaneuses.fait: This canvas by Jean-François Millet, shown at the Salon the very year it was painted, is now kept at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris.

crepe-suzette.fait: These crêpes with orange or tangerine butter are usually served flambéed, although, according to some cookbooks, the original recipe serves them unflambéed.

dame-licorne.fait: This set brings together six tapestries from the early Renaissance, kept in Paris at the Musée de Cluny, the national museum of the Middle Ages.

creme-cassis.fait: This blood-red liqueur made from blackcurrants is the essential ingredient of kir, where it is usually mixed with Bourgogne Aligoté.

tapenade.fait: This Provençal preparation of olives crushed in a mortar takes its name from capers, called “tapeno” in Provençal.

galoubet.fait: This Provençal recorder has only three holes and is played with one hand, accompanied by a percussion instrument such as the tambourin.

tapisserie-aubusson.fait: After the crisis between the wars, this craft of the Creuse enjoyed a revival thanks to the arrival of Jean Lurçat in 1939.

confit-canard.fait: This traditional specialty of the cuisine of southwestern France has an equally regional sister: goose confit.

baeckeoffe.fait: Its Alsatian name means “bread oven”: marinated meats and potatoes simmer, tightly covered, for more than 24 hours in an earthenware dish.

festival-interceltique.fait: Born from a competition of bagadoù in 1971, this Breton festival brings together dozens of groups from Celtic countries and regions every August.

far-breton.fait: This Breton pastry, “farz forn” in Breton, is made with eggs, flour, milk and lightly salted butter, sometimes with prunes or rum.

hotel-invalides.fait: Louis XIV had it built for the disabled soldiers of his armies: it still takes them in, next to the tomb of Napoleon I.

canal-du-midi.fait: To supply this canal linking Toulouse to the Mediterranean, Pierre-Paul Riquet brought water from the Montagne Noire to the Seuil de Naurouze.

rocamadour.fait: In this Marian town clinging to a cliff, pilgrims still sometimes climb on their knees the great staircase leading to the Black Virgin.

alignements-carnac.fait: These nearly 3,000 standing stones, spread over sites that now seem isolated, formed a visually continuous whole in the Neolithic.

place-stanislas.fait: It is not its size that makes this square in Nancy original, but its role: linking two formerly independent districts.

porter.fait: Its English name means “carrier” or “street porter”: it was by modifying this beer that Guinness gave rise to stouts.

beef-wellington.fait: This beef tenderloin, covered with foie gras and duxelles, is baked wrapped in puff pastry, then served in slices.
